fonti.title: The Pyramid of Meidum (Egyptian Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities)

funzione_ufficiale: Royal tomb
note: Now in ruins, it originally stood about 49 m tall and lies northeast of Djoser's step pyramid.

datazione_ufficiale: Late 26th–25th century BCE; the proposed dates for Sahure's reign vary
funzione_ufficiale: Royal tomb
note: The original height is given as between 47 and 48 m and the base side as between 78.5 and 78.75 m; it is now in ruins, with five of the six inner steps remaining.

funzione_ufficiale: Royal tomb
note: Begun as a 52 m step pyramid, it was meant to become a true pyramid of 72.8 m but was left unfinished; Wikipedia's list gives 54 m instead.

datazione_ufficiale: Mid-25th century BCE (reign c. 2445–2421 BCE, one of the proposed dates)
funzione_ufficiale: Royal tomb
note: Originally 51.68 m tall, it is now reduced to a heap of rubble, and its mortuary temple has an unusual L-shaped plan.

funzione_ufficiale: Royal tomb
note: Now in ruins, it originally stood 43 m tall and is the first pyramid with the Pyramid Texts inscribed inside.

funzione_ufficiale: Royal tomb
note: Originally 52.5 m tall, it now looks like a small hill and is the second known pyramid with the Pyramid Texts.

funzione_ufficiale: Royal tomb
note: It stands in the southern part of Saqqara and measures 52.4 m according to Wikipedia's entry, with no separate figure for its current height.

nome: Pyramid of Amenemhat III at Hawara
funzione_ufficiale: Royal tomb
note: It has a mudbrick core, once covered in limestone that was later stripped away, and the nearby mortuary temple is thought to be the basis of the Labyrinth described by Herodotus.

fonti.title: The Pyramid of Amenemhet III at Hawara

tipo: Egyptian royal pyramid, now in ruins
funzione_ufficiale: Royal tomb
note: Originally about 75 m tall, it suffered serious structural problems because it was built on clay unsuited to bearing its weight and prone to water seepage.

datazione_ufficiale: Early 19th century BCE; reign proposed between c. 1900 and 1870 BCE
funzione_ufficiale: Royal tomb
note: The true entrance was hidden beneath a tomb on the southeast side rather than on the north side, apparently to deter thieves.

regione: Northern Sudan, near the Fourth Cataract
funzione_ufficiale: Royal necropolis of Napatan kings and queens
note: Height and base refer to the pyramid of Taharqa, the oldest and largest at the site, which sources give as 40 or 50 m, or as 160–180 feet.

regione: Northern State, between the Third and Fourth Cataracts
datazione_ufficiale: Main use c. 860–650 BCE; pyramid Ku.1 c. 325 BCE
funzione_ufficiale: Kushite royal necropolis
note: The height of about 35 m is the original height of Ku.1, the largest pyramid at the site, built around 325 BCE and never used for a royal burial.

fonti.title: El-Kurru: The Pyramid (University of Michigan, Kelsey Museum)

funzione_ufficiale: Tomb of Gaius Cestius
note: Faced in Luna marble, it was built along the Via Ostiense under the terms of Cestius's will and later incorporated into the Aurelian Walls.

fonti.title: Pyramid of Caius Cestius (Soprintendenza Speciale di Roma)
The Pyramid of Caius Cestius (Turismo Roma)

funzione_ufficiale: Religious center of Elam, dedicated to Inshushinak and Napirisha
note: Founded by King Untash-Napirisha, the ziggurat was about 53 m tall and now measures 24.75 m.

funzione_ufficiale: Ziggurat dedicated to Enlil
note: Built by Kurigalzu I about 30 km west of Baghdad, it has a base of 69 x 67 m, and the 52 m given is its current height; the original height is not recorded.

datazione_ufficiale: 6th century BCE, on an older tower from the 2nd millennium BCE
funzione_ufficiale: Ziggurat dedicated to Nabu
note: Completed by Nebuchadnezzar with seven terraces, it reached 70 m and today preserves 52, with a casing that brought the base to 78 x 78 m.

datazione_ufficiale: Not dated directly by the sources; attributed to Gwanggaeto (reigned 391–412) or his son Jangsu
funzione_ufficiale: Royal tomb
note: A Goguryeo stone tomb with sides of about 75 m and a height of 11 m, it is part of the UNESCO site of the ancient kingdom, and its attribution to a king remains a hypothesis.

fonti.title: The Tombs of Goguryeo (World History Encyclopedia)
Capital Cities and Tombs of the Ancient Koguryo Kingdom (UNESCO)

nome_locale: ប្រាសាទបក្សីចាំក្រុង
funzione_ufficiale: Temple dedicated to Shiva
note: The four-tiered laterite pyramid is 13 m tall, rising to 23 m with the brick tower on top.

funzione_ufficiale: Temple dedicated to Shiva
note: Founded by Indravarman I, the five-tiered pyramid measures 67 x 65 m at the base, its top level rises 14 m above the ground, and the central shrine is 15 m tall.

fonti.title: The Roluos Group: Bakong (The Angkor Guide)

funzione_ufficiale: State temple dedicated to Shiva
note: The state temple of Rajendravarman, it has three tiers a little over 12 m tall on a 50 m base, and a summit platform of 35 m.

nome_locale: ប្រាសាទតាកែវ
funzione_ufficiale: Temple dedicated to Shiva
note: The five-tiered pyramid, left unfinished until the reign of Suryavarman I, is 21.5 m tall and the central tower reaches 45 m.

datazione_ufficiale: Attributed to field-clearing work between the 1930s and 1960s, with no in-depth scientific research
funzione_ufficiale: Pile of stones removed from sugar cane fields
note: News sources describe seven basalt cairns, one 10 m tall according to African Arguments, while Atlas Obscura puts them at around 20 m.

fonti.title: Mauritius: How did the pyramids of Plaine Magnien get there? (African Arguments)

datazione_ufficiale: Between 1803 and 1812 according to the most recent research
funzione_ufficiale: Unknown
note: The top is lost, and the original height of about 30 feet comes from a single popular source, while the elevation is given as 455 m by a hiking site and 430 m by that source.

funzione_ufficiale: Probable funerary monument, tomb or cenotaph
note: The 22.65 m is the current height of what remains, the original height is not given, and the monument has no inner chambers.

datazione_ufficiale: 8th century CE; the city flourished between 600 and 1200 CE
funzione_ufficiale: Ritual building: the deep niches evoke caves, regarded as passages to the underworld
leggende_locali: For the Totonacs, twelve ancient storm gods called Tajín still inhabit the ruins.
note: It has seven levels and 365 niches on the original structure; the side of the base is 35 m according to Wikipedia and 26 m according to World History Encyclopedia.

tipo: Double step pyramid on a platform
datazione_ufficiale: After 1325, rebuilt six times; almost entirely destroyed by the Spanish in 1521
funzione_ufficiale: Main temple, dedicated to Huitzilopochtli and Tlaloc
note: Originally about 90 feet (27 m) tall according to the Metropolitan Museum; only ruins remain today, and the base measured about 100 by 80 m.

fonti.title: Tenochtitlan: Templo Mayor, The Metropolitan Museum of Art

datazione_ufficiale: Core from the Late Preclassic, with expansions in the Early and Late Classic up to the 8th century CE
funzione_ufficiale: Pyramid temple with a palace on top in the Late Classic and Tomb 4 in Structure 2B
note: It rises above 45 m on a square base 120 m on each side, and the coordinates are those Wikipedia gives for the site, not for the individual structure.

tipo: Step pyramid with a summit temple
funzione_ufficiale: Main structure of Cobá, with a temple on top reached by a staircase of 120 steps
note: It is 42 m tall, has a central staircase of 120 steps, and the coordinates refer to the Cobá site.

datazione_ufficiale: Built during the city's heyday, occupied from about 500 BCE to 900 CE; no specific date
funzione_ufficiale: Closes off the Great Plaza; two small ceremonial mounds on top
note: According to INAH it is the tallest building in the city, at 40 m high and about 140 m on a side, and it has carved stelae at the bottom and at the corners.

tipo: Five-tiered pyramid with a summit temple
datazione_ufficiale: Not dated individually; Tula Grande reached its peak between 900 and 1150 CE
funzione_ufficiale: Temple dedicated to Quetzalcoatl as Lord of the Dawn (Tlahuizcalpantecuhtli)
note: The height of about 30 feet (9 m) comes from a single travel guide, and the carved warriors on top, about 4.6 m tall, supported the temple roof.

datazione_ufficiale: Before 900 CE; the site's main building phase was in the Epiclassic (700–900 CE)
funzione_ufficiale: Platform temple with reliefs of the feathered serpent and of tributary cities
popolazione_ufficiale_associata: Xochicalco, with influences from Teotihuacan and the Maya
note: The base measures 19.6 by 21 m, and the temple was restored by Leopoldo Batres in 1910.

tipo: Six-level pyramid in the talud-tablero style
funzione_ufficiale: Religious and political center
note: More than a hundred sacrificial burials, mostly of men, are associated with the pyramid and linked to its construction and dedication.

fonti.title: Temple of the Feathered Serpent, Teotihuacan, Wikipedia

tipo: Double pyramid with a serpent wall
datazione_ufficiale: First phase around 1250, last between 1450 and 1500 according to INAH; Wikipedia gives 1299 and 1507
funzione_ufficiale: Double temple dedicated to Tlaloc and Huitzilopochtli
note: The last phase measures 62 by 50 m, and the base is surrounded by a platform with about 140 serpent sculptures; sources count six or seven building phases.

funzione_ufficiale: Marks the reign of Yik'in Chan K'awiil and may be his funerary temple
note: It measures 64.6 m from the platform to the top of the roof comb, while Wikipedia's summary box gives 70 m.

tipo: Pyramidal complex with palaces and temples
datazione_ufficiale: Founded at the end of the Late Preclassic, raised in the Late Classic, abandoned around 900 CE
funzione_ufficiale: Royal residence and complex with four palaces and three temples
note: At 43 m tall, it is described as the tallest man-made structure in Belize, and the coordinates are those of the site.

datazione_ufficiale: First phase around 100 BCE; Late Classic appearance around 700 CE
funzione_ufficiale: Focal point of the site's first major plaza group
note: At 33 m tall, its initial phase dates to about 100 BCE according to the archaeologists David Pendergast and Elizabeth Graham.

fonti.title: What Do We Know about Lamanai?, York University

datazione_ufficiale: Phase A-6-2nd around 800 CE; no date for the final phase
funzione_ufficiale: Shrine, administrative center and elite residence
note: About 40 m tall, it is the second-tallest Maya structure in Belize, and the frieze visible today is a reproduction.

datazione_ufficiale: From about 426 CE to the final phase of 775–776 CE
funzione_ufficiale: Funerary and cult monument dedicated to the founder Yax K'uk' Mo'
note: It rises about 100 feet (30 m) above the Great Plaza and 20 m above the West Court, and encloses the Rosalila temple, buried around 700 CE.

datazione_ufficiale: Great Pyramid around 500 CE; first Lima occupation, c. 400–700 CE
funzione_ufficiale: Ceremonial and administrative center
popolazione_ufficiale_associata: Lima culture, later reused for Wari burials
note: The pyramid is 22 m tall, or 25 m according to another source, in the Miraflores district of Lima.

tipo: Adobe pyramid temple with platforms and plazas
datazione_ufficiale: At least five building phases between about 300 and 600 CE
funzione_ufficiale: Ceremonial and religious temple
note: The complex covers about 300 by 250 m, with three platforms and four plazas, while Structurae gives 80 by 60 m without clarifying which part that refers to.

tipo: Two adobe pyramids and a low platform
datazione_ufficiale: Site 50–700 CE; platform and first pyramid before 300 CE, second pyramid around 700 CE
funzione_ufficiale: Sacred and political center, with royal tombs
note: The two pyramids measure 35 and 37 m, the site covers 29.5 hectares at an elevation of 83 to 102 m, and the tomb of the Lord of Sipán was found here.

tipo: Step pyramid with a rectangular plan
datazione_ufficiale: 200–1470 CE in the official visitor circuit; built in the Ychma period, 1100–1470 CE
funzione_ufficiale: Building that housed the deity and idol of Pachacamac
leggende_locali: According to a coastal myth, Pachacamac defeated the rival creator god Con, who had stopped the rains to punish humanity.
note: It measures 120 by 65 m with 7 m of visible architecture, and is the only building in the sanctuary with polychrome wall paintings; the coordinates are those of the site.

fonti.title: Trabajos de conservación en el Templo Pintado, Santuario de Pachacamac

datazione_ufficiale: Seven building phases from about 200 CE, abandoned around 650 CE
funzione_ufficiale: Ceremonial, ritual and funerary temple
note: About 30 m tall on a base of about 330 feet (100 m) per side, it holds the burial of the Lady of Cao; the elevation of 28 m is that of the complex.

tipo: Platform mound with two summit mounds
funzione_ufficiale: Burials, temples and ceremonies
note: The main mound is 11 m tall and reaches about 18 m with the secondary mounds, on a base of about 230 by 133 m covering eight acres.

datazione_ufficiale: Ground preparation radiocarbon-dated between 1450 and 1250 BCE
funzione_ufficiale: Interpreted as a bird effigy or as the cosmological center of the site
note: At 22 m tall on a base of about 215 by 200 m, it is not a true pyramid but a T-shaped mound, and the coordinates are those of the site.

datazione_ufficiale: 10th century CE according to the National Park Service; main occupation 950–1150 CE
funzione_ufficiale: Seat of the village chief
note: 55 feet (17 m) tall, it was built in four successive phases, and the coordinates are those of the park.

fonti.title: Great Temple Mound Complex, National Park Service
Ocmulgee Mounds National Historical Park, Wikipedia

datazione_ufficiale: Not dated individually; site occupied from about 600 BCE to about 1450 CE
funzione_ufficiale: Residence of the rulers and shrine
note: According to Mexico News Daily it is 31.5 m tall, and the coordinates are those of the site.

funzione_ufficiale: Polynesian temple, topped with a stone fish and a wooden bird
popolazione_ufficiale_associata: Tahitians, commissioned by Purea and Amo
note: It originally stood 17 m tall on a base of 81 by 26.5 m with 11 terraces according to the Tahiti tourism board, while other sources give 14–15 m.

fonti.title: Coral dating and Polynesian temples, Phys.org

datazione_ufficiale: Probably 1100–1400 CE, out of use by 1700–1800 CE
funzione_ufficiale: Central ceremonial site; exact function uncertain
leggende_locali: Palauli's oral traditions link the mound to Lilomaiava, one of the supreme titles of Savai'i, as the foundation of his residence, a gathering place for chiefs, or an ancient burial site.
note: About 12 m tall on the south side and 7 m on the north, with a base of about 65 by 60 m, but the World Monuments Fund considers the construction date unknown.

fonti.title: What is the Pulemelei Mound?, Samoa Observer
